item.description: Broussonetia × kazinoki, a hybrid of B. monoica and B. papyrifera, is a main resource from which traditional paper is made and medicine is obtained. Due to extensive morphological variation, identification from parental species, using morphological characteristics alone is difficult, especially during non-flowering seasons. This study developed a 26 S rDNA-based cleaved amplified polymorphic sequence (CAPS) marker to enable precise identification even when morphological characteristics are...

item.title: Nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation for competing risks frailty models
item.description: In clustered competing risks data, both event times within the same cluster and competing events are often correlated. This dependency can be modeled using cluster-specific frailties. This paper considers both hierarchical likelihood and nonparametric likelihood methods for fitting the so-called shared bivariate frailty model, a special case of the cause-specific competing risks frailty model with two causes of events, to clustered competing risks data. For this purpose, it first theoretically...

item.title: Prolonged hospitalization following head and neck cancer surgery: risk factors, clinical outcomes, and strategies for care optimization
item.description: CONCLUSION: Prolonged hospitalization after HNC surgery is associated with adverse oncologic outcomes which may reflect underlying disease severity, and is primarily driven by postoperative complications, particularly flap-related complications, the most important and modifiable determinant of prolonged LOS.

item.title: PhenoFECT: A Python package for forecasting and exploring plant phenology under climate change
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PhenoFECT is a versatile tool for accurate forecasting, exploration, and visualization across diverse open meteorological data. Exploring data using PhenoFECT revealed that the CDM can be influenced by geographic features and global climate phenomena.

item.title: Longitudinal associations between loneliness and cognitive performance in older adults: evidence from intensive longitudinal assessment
item.description: CONCLUSION: Baseline cognitive performance did not predict subsequent changes in loneliness. When examined in the other direction, associations between loneliness and cognition appeared limited and domain-specific, with only associative memory showing a longitudinal association with baseline loneliness.

item.description: A diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder poses significant emotional and practical challenges for parents. Although diagnostic resolution and parent activation have been examined separately, little is known about whether parents' psychological adjustment relates to active caregiving and, in turn, to child outcomes. This study tested: (1) a mediation model linking diagnostic resolution to child emotional-behavioral difficulties through parent activation; (2) psychometric properties of the Italian...

item.title: Biomaterial-assisted culture of mesenchymal stem cells for enhanced extracellular vesicle production and cartilage regeneration: a systematic review
item.description: Articular cartilage has limited self-repair capacity, prompting interest in cell-free therapies such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This systematic review assessed whether MSCs cultured with biomaterials produce more EVs, and EVs with greater chondrogenic or cartilage-regenerative efficacy, than MSCs in conventional culture. The publications were searched on PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO (2016-2026), and the synthesis of the evidence was done narratively,...

item.title: Chronic disease burden and health-related quality of life among missouri adults
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Greater chronic disease burden was associated with poorer physical and mental HRQoL among Missouri adults. Adding HRQoL assessment to chronic disease surveillance and clinical follow-up may help identify functional limitations and mental health needs that are not apparent from diagnoses alone.

item.title: Sonodynamic Therapy in Periodontitis: From Mechanisms to Biomaterial-Based Innovations
item.description: Periodontitis is a common chronic inflammatory disease driven by pathogenic biofilms, leading to progressive periodontal tissue destruction and systemic health risks. Conventional therapies often fail to eradicate biofilms in deep periodontal pockets, promote antimicrobial resistance and offer limited regenerative potential. Although SDT has emerged as a promising alternative, its clinical efficacy is constrained by several material- and microenvironment-related barriers that have not been...

item.title: Early Assessment of Circulating Tumor Cells and Their PD-L1 Expression as Predictive Biomarkers in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients Treated with Immunotherapy: An Exploratory Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Baseline CTCs levels tended to be associated with clinical outcomes, whereas PD-L1 expression on CTCs was not. Early evaluation of changes in these two parameters did not improve outcome prediction under ICI treatment. Larger studies with longer follow-up and more in-depth analyses are warranted to further define the prognostic and predictive value of CTC-based biomarkers.

item.title: The "Invisible Killer" of Neurodegeneration: Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Disorders, Mechanisms, Emerging Pathways and Therapeutic Strategies
item.description: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease (PD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), Huntington's disease (HD), multiple sclerosis (MS), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) place substantial burden on global public health. Mounting evidence identifies mitochondrial dysfunction as a central contributor to neuronal damage and progressive brain functional decline. As a narrative review, this work aims to dissect mitochondrial‑associated pathological features across these major...

item.title: Responsible use of new antibiotics for critically ill patients suffering from infections due to carbapenem-resistant organisms-a narrative review for an enablement strategy
item.description: Infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative (MDR-GN) bacteria, particularly carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs), constitute a significant burden in critically ill patients (CIPs). A multidisciplinary, collaborative approach is essential for responsible antibiotic use in CIPs, balancing the necessity for effective treatment with mitigation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). While the efficacy of existing antibiotics against CROs is increasingly limited due to resistance development...

item.title: Primary Hepatic Neuroblastoma: A Case Report of a Solitary Liver Mass in an Adolescent Male
item.description: Primary hepatic neuroblastoma (PHN) is an exceptionally rare subtype of neuroblastoma. Neuroblastoma typically arises in tissues of the sympathetic nervous system, and hepatic metastases are more common than PHN. We present a 12-year-old male who presented with abdominal discomfort. Imaging revealed hepatomegaly with a solitary mass in segment V of the liver. After total resection, histopathological analysis identified a poorly differentiated neuroblastoma with a low mitotic-karyorrhectic index...

item.title: First-year changes in mental health, lifestyle behaviors, and social support among international students at a Japanese university
item.description: CONCLUSION: Monitoring changes in sleep duration and interpersonal tension after enrollment may enhance academic and mental health support for international students.

item.description: LAF-Stp xenopeptides (XPs) comprising lipoamino fatty acid (LAF) units connected with the tetraethylene pentamine derived polyamino acid Stp were identified as a novel class of amphiphilic mRNA carriers. A 'chameleon-like' polarity switch is observed upon transition from neutral physiological to endosomal acidic pH. Protonation of the lipidic tertiary amine of LAF results in an ~2 log unit change in the octanol/water partition coefficient (logD), consistent with all-atom molecular dynamics...

item.title: Bilateral exchange in synthetic biology: experiences, challenges, and opportunities for training and research
item.description: Synthetic biology and the emerging field of biomanufacturing provide new research concepts that should be incorporated into the training of the next generation of scientists. Key elements of synthetic biology are the standardization, modularization, and characterization of biological parts. Defined parts can be assembled into functional transcription units to pathways of multiple units, chromosomes, and/or whole genomes. Here, we highlight the importance of global exchange and state-of-the-art...

item.title: Aptamers in Brucellosis: Diagnostic Advances, Current Challenges and Future Perspectives
item.description: Brucellosis, caused by Brucella species, is a major zoonosis with global health and economic burdens. Conventional diagnostics suffer from slow culture, biosafety risks, cross-reactivity, and equipment dependence. Aptamers, synthetic single-stranded oligonucleotides selected via Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX), offer promising alternatives to antibodies. This review focuses primarily on recent advances in aptamer-based diagnostic technologies for brucellosis....

item.title: Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) Mapping and Visualization of Pre-Implementation Determinants for Sepsis Care Transitions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholders identified complexity emerged across technical, structural, and policy domains as both an innovation feature and contextual determinants of sepsis care transitions. CFIR mapping and visualization provided a structured approach to characterizing pre-implementation complexity in sepsis care transitions. Examining determinant representation and cross-domain interconnectedness may help identify cross-cutting, potentially high-leverage implementation needs and inform...

item.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy
item.description: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

item.title: Physiological and multiomics analyses on photosynthesis and carbon utilization reveal biochemical carbon-concentrating mechanisms in Hygrophilla difformis under submergence
item.description: Hygrophila difformis is an ornamental amphibious plant that develops distinct terrestrial (shallow-serrated) and submerged (deep-lobed) leaf forms in response to environmental conditions. Although previous studies have reported bicarbonate (HCO₃^(-)) utilization and highlighted the involvement of carbonic anhydrase in inorganic carbon uptake, the photosynthetic strategy and carbon assimilation pathway operating under submergence remain unclear. Here, we applied an integrated framework combining...

item.title: Enhanced Efficacy of Thalidomide-Based Cocktail With Transarterial Chemoembolization in the Management of Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Center Cohort Study
item.description: This retrospective study was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of adding a thalidomide-based cocktail (the TCC cocktail-comprising thalidomide, carmofur, and compound mylabris capsule) to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in real-world practice. Data from 433 unresectable HCC patients treated with TACE at four hospitals were collected (from March 2014 to May 2018, followed up to July 2023) and overall survival (OS), overall response...

item.title: "You Can Talk to Me About Your Pregnancy": Exploring the Perspectives of Health-Care Providers on Cannabis Use During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding
item.description: Exploring health-care providers' perspectives on cannabis use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is essential for improving patient-provider communication on these topics. Twenty medical providers caring for pregnant individuals were recruited to participate in semi-structured key informant interviews, which asked about strategies and challenges caring for pregnant individuals using cannabis. Health-care providers worried about the harmfulness of cannabis during the perinatal period, short...

item.title: Integrating local and landscape management promotes biodiversity, multifunctionality and yields in tropical agroforests
item.description: Reconciling food production and biodiversity conservation requires socio-ecologically viable agroecosystems. To meet this goal, tropical agroforestry must balance yield-biodiversity trade-offs through local and landscape-level management. By integrating assessments of multi-taxa diversity, biocontrol, pollination, crop pests, soil fertility, microclimate, and yield in Amazonian cacao agroforests, we identified ecological-economic synergies. Yield gains were not associated with species loss....

item.title: Communication and shared decision-making for anti-amyloid therapy in early Alzheimer's disease: An exploratory qualitative study of real-world audio-recorded clinical encounters
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Anti-amyloid therapies (AATs) for Alzheimer's disease (AD) offer modest slowing of cognitive decline but involve meaningful risks, burdens, and uncertainty. Decisions about AAT are preference sensitive and optimally guided by shared decision making (SDM), yet little is known about how these conversations unfold in real-world clinical practice.

item.title: Non-analog environments supported early Homo sapiens in southern Africa 200 000 years ago
item.description: In our species' evolutionary history, the type of environments in which we evolved can provide crucial details about early human adaptive capacities. Such environments might not exist under current climatic and ecological conditions. Reconstructing palaeohydrology and vegetation using multiple proxies at human fossil sites in South Africa provides insights into local conditions at a high level of detail. This paper presents a plant n-alkane stable isotope record for Florisbad and Lombard's...

item.title: When are Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks Good Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries? A Data-Driven Analysis
item.description: Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium-ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs lack generality, and the suitability of these materials as alternatives to conventional electrodes remains poorly resolved. Here, we map structure-electrode-function relationships across 1099 experimentally synthesized 2D COFs from the CoRE COF database by developing a...

item.title: Single-Cell Insights Into Pathogenic Profile of Orchitis and SREBP2-Associated Cholesterol Dysregulation in Spermatogenic Failure
item.description: Orchitis, a testicular inflammation often triggered by infection, is a major cause of male infertility due to disruption of the testicular immune microenvironment and progressive loss of germ cells. Currently, no effective or targeted therapies are available. Here, we profile 66,147 single-cell transcriptomes from testes of orchitis patients and healthy controls, complemented by histological validation. We observe profound remodeling of testicular cell composition, with marked infiltration of...

item.title: NDFIP2 Suppresses Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through DDX3X-Dependent R-Loop Remodeling and GNG13 Transcriptional Activation
item.description: Distant metastasis remains the leading cause of colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Integrating RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) profiling and clinical validation, we identified NDFIP2 as significantly downregulated in metastatic CRC. Functionally, NDFIP2 loss drove epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), stemness, and metastasis via PI3K/AKT hyperactivation. Mechanistically, NDFIP2 serves as an adaptor recruiting the E3 ligase NEDD4...

item.title: Integrated Multiomic Analysis Reveals an EBV-Associated MIF-SPP1<sup>+</sup> Macrophage Axis Linking Tumor Stemness and Immune Dysfunction in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
item.description: Elucidating how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) shapes tumor-immune interactions is important for improving therapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This multi-cohort analysis integrates single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data with multiplex immunofluorescence and functional assays. Single-cell profiling identifies stemness-associated epithelial states and enrichment of SPP1^(+) tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in EBV^(+) NPC. SPP1^(+) TAM abundance is associated with...

item.title: MAGI3 Acts as an Intestinal Epithelial Gatekeeper in Inflammation-Associated Colorectal Cancer by Suppressing the STAT3-CCL2 Axis and TAM-Mediated Immunosuppression
item.description: Chronic intestinal inflammation is a major driver of colorectal cancer (CRC). As the mucosal barrier's frontline sentinel, the intestinal epithelium initiates the inflammation-to-cancer transition. However, the early cell-intrinsic events that convert inflammatory responses into a sustained pro-tumorigenic program remain unclear. In this study, we identify MAGI3 as an intestinal epithelial guardian progressively lost during inflammation-associated colorectal tumorigenesis. Low MAGI3 correlates...

item.title: Loss of Lepr in Fibroblasts Drives Tumor Development by Promoting Macrophage Infiltration
item.description: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are critical regulators of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, yet the mechanisms governing their functional plasticity and state transitions remain incompletely understood. Here, we uncover a tumor-driven fibroblast state transition in CRC characterized by loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression and acquisition of pro-inflammatory features. We show that cooperative TNFα and TGFβ signaling drives this reprogramming, accompanied by repression of the...

item.title: Adsorption Technology for Lithium Extraction: Recent Progress and Future Perspectives
item.description: Lithium, a critical enabler of the new energy paradigm, has made its efficient recovery a strategic priority worldwide. Among direct lithium extraction (DLE) technologies, adsorption stands out for its superior Mg/Li selectivity and low energy intensity when processing salt-lake brines. This review critically surveys recent breakthroughs in inorganic ion sieves, covering anion-dependent behavior and magnetic functionalization of Li/Al-LDHs, synergistic doping-coating strategies for Mn-based...

item.title: Defining Core Functions and Forms for the Implementation of Pharmacogenomics Testing in Primary Care
item.description: Pharmacogenomics (PGx), utilizing a patient's DNA to individualize medication prescribing, minimizes adverse events and improves patient outcomes. However, the integration of PGx into primary care remains sparse. PGx testing encompasses multiple components and can be considered a complex health intervention. We conducted an in-person workshop with early adopters from the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network Implementation Working Group, followed by qualitative interviews with key opinion...

item.title: Lead poisoning and its clinical manifestation in opium users: a case series
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case series emphasizes the importance of awareness among both opium users and medical staff regarding the risks related to lead poisoning due to contaminated opium. Patients should be informed about the potential contamination of opium, which can cause serious gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms, and even death. Healthcare providers should maintain a high index of suspicion for lead poisoning in opium-addicted patients presenting with compatible symptoms, ensuring early...

item.title: Feasibility of acceptance and commitment therapy for repetitive negative thinking versus internet-based CBT: a pilot randomised controlled trial in Swedish primary care among patients with anxiety, depression and stress
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The small sample size and high iCBT non-completion limit between-group comparisons. Further investigation of recruitment, treatment engagement, and patient and therapist experiences is needed before determining whether and how to proceed to a full-scale RCT.

item.title: Diffusion-weighted imaging reversal after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke: associations with white matter hyperintensities and cerebral microbleeds
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of an association between baseline WMH volume or CMB presence and early DWI lesion reversal or hemorrhagic complications following reperfusion therapy in this cohort. These findings provide no evidence that these two chronic MRI markers are major determinants of early infarct tissue reversibility. Larger multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive small-vessel disease phenotyping and long-term follow-up are warranted.

item.title: Layer-specific quantitative analysis of accommodation in the human lens using long-range OCT and machine learning
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a map of lenticular deformation during accommodation, identifying the cortical C4 zones and the lens nucleus as the primary deformation compartments. In contrast, the peripheral cortex remains relatively passive. These findings demonstrate that accommodation cannot be fully described using global lens metrics alone. Therefore, biomechanical and optical models should incorporate cortical and nuclear behavior instead of treating the lens as a homogeneous structure....

item.title: Seasonal dynamics and prognostic determinants of respiratory failure in critically ill adults: a multicenter retrospective observational study in Northern China
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study revealed nonlinear and lagged associations between meteorological factors and monthly respiratory failure admissions, with the highest admission counts observed in winter, followed by spring. In the fitted random forest model, clinical and physiological features contributed more to mortality predictions than meteorological variables.

item.title: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies in solid tumors: clinical trial updates from ASCO 2026
item.description: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies integrate immune checkpoint blockade and VEGF inhibition within a single molecule, offering a potential strategy to overcome angiogenesis-associated immune resistance. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy over tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extending survival evidence to an...

item.title: Aggression in Psychiatric High and Intensive Care Wards: A Mixed Methods Study of Incidence and Professionals' Reflections
item.description: This mixed methods study investigates aggression in acute psychiatric care, focusing on both incidence and professional reflections across 23 High and Intensive Care wards in the Netherlands. Using a sequential explanatory design, quantitative data on aggressive incidents were collected over 12 months and followed by qualitative focus groups with nurses and team leaders. Aggression, predominantly physical and often targeting staff, was frequently reported, while the cause of incidents was...

item.title: Dual targeting of ACSS2 and ACLY by a novel inhibitor S8588 suppresses oncogenic lipogenesis and overcomes metabolic compensation in oral squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: Metabolic reprogramming, particularly enhanced lipid anabolism, is a hallmark of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet effective therapies targeting this process remain lacking. Here, we identify concurrent activation of acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2) and ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) as a cooperative metabolic driver of OSCC progression. Whereas previous efforts have focused on single-enzyme inhibition, we show that ACSS2 and ACLY form a compensatory network that sustains lipid anabolism and...

item.title: Sex- and age-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology on T2-weighted MR imaging: a population-based study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Using automated, large-scale MRI, this study characterizes age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology in a large population-based cohort. These findings provide a comprehensive, normative reference of age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology across the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine, offering a framework to support clinical interpretation, spine research, and surgical planning.

item.title: In vivo frataxin expression of a triplex purified minicircle
item.description: Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by (GAA•TTC)(n) repeat expansions in the Frataxin (FXN) gene, resulting in reduced expression of Frataxin, a mitochondrial protein essential for energy production and iron-sulfur cluster assembly. Minicircles (MCs) are non-viral DNA vectors offering improved safety and efficiency over conventional plasmids. item.title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach
item.description: Persistent fever after initiating intravenous antibiotics is common in hospitalized patients with cancer and often leads to additional imaging and antimicrobial escalation. Early identification of patients unlikely to remain febrile could provide additional information during clinical reassessment. We developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict persistent fever 48-72 h after antibiotic initiation using electronic health records from two academic hospitals. Adult cancer...

item.title: Spatial multi-omics of mouse incisor mesenchyme reveals metabolic remodeling during the MSC-to-TAC transition
item.description: The continuously growing mouse incisor provides a useful model for investigating stem cell niche organization and the MSC-to-TAC transition because it contains spatially distinct mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-enriched and transit-amplifying cell (TAC)-enriched compartments and abundant TAC populations. item.title: Cannabinoid receptor type 1 availability in individuals with a history of childhood trauma: a positron emission tomography study
item.description: Early life adversity has a lasting impact on the endocannabinoid (eCB) system based on animal models. However, the impact of early life adversity, such as childhood trauma (CT), on the eCB system has not been thoroughly studied. We assessed the availability of cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) in individuals with CT compared to healthy controls without CT (HCs). Cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) availability was compared in adults with CT (N = 22) and age- and sex-matched HCs (n = 22), using...

item.title: State-dependent effects of rTMS on cognitive function in bipolar II disorder: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory trial did not provide statistically robust evidence that concurrent complex cognitive engagement enhanced the acute working-memory effects of IPL-targeted 10-Hz rTMS in euthymic bipolar II disorder, suggesting that task type, cognitive load, and stimulation-task coupling warrant further systematic optimization in future neuromodulation studies.

item.title: The FKBPL-RPA1 axis regulates DNA damage repair and cellular survival in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the need to identify molecular mechanisms that support tumour cell survival and therapeutic resistance. Here, we identify FK506-binding protein-like (FKBPL) as a novel regulator of the DNA damage repair (DDRR) in HCC. Analysis of public datasets and an HCC tissue microarray demonstrated that FKBPL expression is significantly elevated in HCC tissues compared with normal liver and is associated...

item.title: SIRT3 deficiency triggers mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence to suppress colorectal cancer progression via SLC25A13 acetylation
item.description: Mitochondrial dysfunction is frequently well-known to induce mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MIDAS), a specialized form of cellular senescence marked by a distinct senescent phenotype. Sirtuin-3 (SIRT3) is a key regulator of mitochondrial function through its deacetylase activity, and emerging evidence highlights that its deficiency induces MIDAS in fibroblasts. However, the precise mechanism by which SIRT3 regulates MIDAS, as well as the role of MIDAS in tumorigenesis, remains...

item.description: Vacancy engineering offers an effective route to tailoring Co-based oxygen electrocatalysts, yet vacancy-rich sites can also intensify oxygen-intermediate binding and impede active-site regeneration if their polarized coordination environments are not properly regulated. Herein, a metal-core-buffered vacancy-shell strategy is proposed by coupling ultrasmall metallic Co nanodots with a Co-vacancy-rich CoO(x)/C shell within a conductive mesoporous carbon framework. item.description: No abstract

item.title: Cultural redevelopment and validation of the emotion regulation goals scale - culturally redeveloped version (ERGS-CRV): evidence from Iran
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The ERGS-CRV provides a culturally informed measure of emotion-regulation goals in Iranian adults, with stronger psychometric support for the Pro-Social and Impression Management dimensions, acceptable support for the Performance dimension, and comparatively weaker support for the Pro-Hedonic and Contra-Hedonic dimensions. The findings support its use for research on emotion-regulation motives in Persian-speaking and potentially other non-Western populations.

item.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that compound II8 may serve as a localized prophylactic nasal spray, providing valuable insights for further development of LLPS modulators as next-generation antiviral agents.

item.title: Attenuation of colonic epithelial architectural disruption by 5-aminosalicylic acid in male mice with DSS-induced colitis: Association with reduced gelatinase-related responses
item.description: Structural deterioration of the colonic epithelium contributes to barrier impairment during intestinal inflammation. We investigated whether 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) modifies epithelial injury and gelatinase-related responses during DSS-induced colonic inflammation. Twenty-four male C57BL/6 mice were divided equally among vehicle control, DSS, and DSS + 5-ASA conditions. item.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae
item.description: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8^(T) and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). item.title: High-sugar foods and breast cancer risk from the Health Examinees study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher consumption of high-sugar foods was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, whereas fruit intake was not. These findings suggest that sugar sources, rather than total sugar intake alone, may be important when considering dietary strategies for breast cancer prevention.

item.description: Copper-cysteine (Cu-Cys) coordination is pervasive in biology, yet how Cu-thiol redox chemistry engages O(2) and translates into protein-level consequences remains incompletely understood. Here, we establish a generalizable protein-based platform that directly captures O(2)-coupled Cu-(II)-Cys redox processes and delineates their structural and functional outcomes. item.description: The monocyte activation test (MAT) detects pyrogenic contamination from the cytokine response of human monocytes and is used as an alternative to the rabbit pyrogen test. PBMC are the reference cell source for the MAT; however, donor variability and limited supply have led to frequent substitutions with the cell lines THP-1, HL-60, and U937. item.title: Platycodon grandiflorus-derived exosome-like nanovesicles drive AMPK-dependent glycolytic beige remodeling to ameliorate obesity
item.description: Obesity is a pandemic with limited therapeutic options. Recent pharmacotherapies are constrained by tolerability, durability, accessibility, and incomplete resolution of adipose tissue dysfunction. Plant-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (ELNs) provide a natural nanoscale therapeutic platform. However, their anti-obesity effects and underlying mechanisms remain unexplored. item.title: Bioinspired Vibration-Induced Droplet Depinning Enables Extraction of Particulates Buried Within Surface Asperities
item.description: Nature has evolved resourceful strategies to sustain hygiene by enabling organisms to dislodge contaminants through the synergy of water-repellent integuments and kinetic energy generated by organismal motion. In this study, an efficient vibration-driven surface cleaning platform for pinned droplet separation is developed, inspired by the natural strategy of Aves that combines water-repellent feathers with compensatory wing flapping motion. item.title: Waveguided, Self-Sensing Sheath-Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
item.description: Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard-to-access environments, while providing integrated self-sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next-generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath-core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. item.title: Anxiety and Mindfulness in the Relationship Between Stress and Depression in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Parallel Mediation Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Mindfulness may be an important psychological factor associated with the relationship between stress and depression in patients with coronary artery disease. Further research is needed to clarify the role of anxiety in this relationship.

item.title: Multi-Omics Profiling of Cigarette Smoke-Associated Changes in Cell Models of Human Liver, Intestine and Lung
item.description: Cigarette smoke is a complex mixture that affects toxicological and pharmacological mechanisms in multiple organs, including liver, intestine, and lung. Therefore, an integrated multi-omics approach was applied to characterize cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced effects across human in vitro models of liver, intestine and lung. Primary human hepatocytes, biopsy-derived intestinal organoids, alveolar A549 cells, primary bronchial and small airway epithelial cells were exposed to CSE and...

item.title: 3D CEST imaging for differentiating malignant and benign prostatic areas: Diagnostic performance relative to DWI
item.description: CONCLUSION: 3D APTw imaging is considered at least as valuable as DWI to distinguish malignant from benign prostatic areas. Combined descriptors could improve diagnostic performance, relative to each sequence alone.

item.title: Pure 6-paradol activates the TRPV1-PGC-1α-FNDC5-irisin axis in cultured myotubes, and a 6-paradol-standardised Aframomum melegueta K. Schum. extract reduces adiposity with relative preservation of lean mass in Korean adults with overweight: an integrated mechanistic and randomised controlled trial investigation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Pure 6-paradol engages a TRPV1-dependent irisin-secretory programme in cultured myotubes. In healthy Korean adults with overweight, the standardised extract produced large-effect adiposity reductions with relative preservation of lean mass and elevated circulating irisin. Because the clinical intervention used a multi-constituent extract, the clinical effects cannot be attributed specifically to 6-paradol, and the serum irisin and PBMC findings do not demonstrate activation of the...

item.title: Clinical outcomes of transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia : a propensity score-matched comparative study
item.description: CONCLUSION: TOA achieved long-term joint survival comparable with that in younger patients, supporting TOA as a joint-preserving option in this age group. However, the sport/recreation score was lower and complications more frequent than in patients aged < 45 years. Preoperative Tönnis grade 2 predicted failure, indicating that joint degeneration, rather than age alone, should guide patient selection.

item.title: Thoracic recurrence after complete gross resection in advanced ovarian cancer: The clinical impact of occult subdiaphragmatic lymphatic invasion
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SLI was independently associated with thoracic recurrence after complete gross resection in AOC, supporting a potential transdiaphragmatic pathway of tumor dissemination.

item.title: Differential roles of translesion synthesis polymerases eta and iota in UV-induced mutagenesis of mouse skin cells and tissues
item.description: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is a human genetic disorder characterized by an increased risk of skin cancer following ultraviolet (UV) exposure and caused by a deficiency in DNA polymerase eta (Polη), a specialized enzyme involved in translesion DNA synthesis (TLS). Polι, a paralog of Polη, exhibits TLS activity on UV-induced DNA lesions in vitro; however, its in vivo function remains unclear. We previously reported that Polη- and Polι-deficient mice exposed to UV irradiation developed...

item.title: SCN1A regulates the cell cycle of mesenchymal stromal cells through APC/C-mediated CCNA2 degradation
item.description: Although voltage-gated sodium channels are known to be expressed in both excitable and non-excitable cells, their roles in non-excitable cells remain poorly understood. Previously, we demonstrated that SCN1A, a voltage-gated sodium channel α-subunit, is involved in the cell cycle in mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) through the degradation of CDK2. Here, we analyzed the role of SCN1A in regulating the degradation of CCNA2, which is essential for CDK2 activation. SCN1A knockdown reduced the CCNA2...

item.title: Synthetic experience augmentation: A two-regime framework for extending LSTM extrapolation in rapid sand filter clogging prediction under water utility consolidation
item.description: Water utility consolidation and capacity expansion require estimates of rapid-filter head loss at unfamiliar filtration velocities. We developed synthetic experience augmentation (SEA) to generate training data for a long short-term memory (LSTM) model from operating records without identifying plant-specific bed parameters. Under laminar conditions, the Kozeny-Carman proportionality scales filtration velocity and head loss at the same target time while retaining measured water-quality...

item.title: Salivary fluoropyrimidine detection and selective Trpm5 mRNA downregulation in taste papillae of male Wistar rats after repeated capecitabine administration
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Repeated capecitabine administration was associated with detectable salivary fluoropyrimidine exposure and selective Trpm5 mRNA downregulation in rat taste papillae. These are measurable oral molecular responses to repeated capecitabine administration.

item.title: Impact of previous decompression technique on operative complexity in redo microvascular decompression for hemifacial spasm
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Redo MVD following a previous transposition procedure was associated with shorter operative and microsurgical times than redo MVD following interposition. These differences appeared to reflect distinct intraoperative pathology and technical demands during reoperation. The initial decompression technique may influence both the intraoperative pathology and surgical complexity of subsequent redo MVD.

item.title: Tiered human health risk assessment of colorants of emerging regulatory concern in household products
item.description: Colorants in household products may contribute to direct human exposure, yet occurrence, migration, and health-risk data remain limited. We investigated 205 visibly colored products, including kitchen cleaning products, disposable wiping products, and disposable food-contact articles, for 40 target colorants using LC-MS/MS and applied a tiered assessment to characterize human health risks and identify chemical-product combinations of potential concern. Ten colorants were detected. Paper napkins...

item.title: Baseline and early post-initiation blood eosinophil counts are associated with eosinophil-related adverse events in dupilumab-treated CRSwNP
item.description: CONCLUSION: The combination of Baseline EC and Peak EC_4w may be useful for assessment of EAE risk.

item.title: Temporal changes in incidence of Shoulder Injury Related to Vaccine Administration (SIRVA) after COVID-19 vaccination
item.description: CONCLUSION: The temporal decline in SIRVA incidence may reflect improvements in the IM injection technique during the COVID-19 mass vaccination, but other factors including changes in reporting behavior should also be considered. Training in proper IM injection techniques, monitoring adverse events, and raising awareness of SIRVA are important to further reduce the incidence of SIRVA.

item.title: Impact of caseload-threshold centralization of intensity-modulated radiotherapy on cancer care regions in Japan: a nationwide ecological geospatial study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Changes in accessibility depend not only on the caseload criterion but also on the geographic unit of centralization. Cancer centralization requires explicit consideration of geographic accessibility.

item.title: Failure patterns after definitive radiotherapy with elective neck irradiation ≤ 40 Gy for head and neck cancer: a multi-institutional study
item.description: To evaluate the efficacy and patterns of failure after definitive radiotherapy (RT) using an elective nodal irradiation (ENI) dose of ≤40 Gy for head and neck cancer. We retrospectively analyzed 290 patients with stage I-IV oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), hypopharyngeal cancer (HPC), or laryngeal cancer (LYC) who underwent definitive RT with an ENI dose of ≤40 Gy at three institutions between 2008 and 2024. A total of 278 patients received 40 Gy of ENI, whereas ENI was omitted in 12 patients...

item.title: Design of Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Based on a Fluorite Structure
item.description: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) is a unique phenomenon in which materials contract upon heating, and thus, there is a strong demand for rational synthetic strategies and the design of giant NTE materials. In tetracyanoborate salts, however, the formation of interpenetrated structures suppresses structural flexibility and limits NTE behavior. Herein, we demonstrated that constructing a fluorite structure is an effective strategy for enhancing NTE through the synthesis of Ba[B(CN)(4)](2) with...

item.title: The evolving burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus in Asia, 1990-2023: A Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide updated regional insights into the heterogeneous epidemiology of T2DM in Asia and may inform targeted prevention and control strategies.

item.title: Contrast sensitivity and imaging findings in patients with idiopathic focal choroidal excavation
item.description: CONCLUSION: Eyes with iFCE showed reduced contrast performance despite preserved visual acuity. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger studies.

item.title: Reply to Qiyi Lin: Regimen-stratified prognostic associations and treatment-by-host-factor interactions in metastatic renal cell carcinoma
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Ultrafast brain MRI at 3 T for suspected acute ischemic stroke: interchangeability of the ultrafast and standard protocols
item.description: CONCLUSION: The ultrafast protocol was interchangeable with the standard protocol for detecting acute ischemic stroke, with reduced scan time and comparable or marginally improved image quality; however, this work-in-progress diffusion-weighted imaging algorithm warrants further validation.

item.title: Geographic variation in diabetes awareness, treatment, and control in India: evidence from a multilevel analysis of national survey data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Care gaps widen sharply toward control. Community-level dominance points to contextual drivers, underscoring the need for locally targeted interventions to strengthen health-system capacity and improve glycaemic control.

item.title: Sesaminol attenuates alcohol-induced colonic senescence in middle-aged mice: potential involvement of the AhR-Nrf2 axis
item.description: As they age, older adults are increasingly susceptible to health decline associated with excessive alcohol consumption, which can accelerate biological aging through cellular stress, senescence-associated responses, and inflammaging. Although sesaminol, a sesame-derived lignan, protects against alcohol-induced colitis in young animals, its effects on alcohol-associated intestinal dysfunction and senescence-related changes in middle-aged animals remain unclear. In this study, middle-aged mice (50...

item.title: Visualization of acetamide-induced large micronucleus formation via nuclear atrophy in rat primary hepatocyte
item.description: Micronuclei are small nuclei that form when chromosomes or fragments fail to segregate into daughter nuclei during cell division. We previously suggested that acetamide induces the formation of large micronuclei through nuclear atrophy in binuclear hepatocytes. In this study, to confirm large micronuclei formation from atrophic nuclei within identical hepatocytes, we established an in vitro model. Large micronuclei formed from rat primary hepatocytes treated with 30 mM acetamide showing...

item.title: Response-Function Driven and Consistency-Gated High-Reliability Urine-Based Cancer Screening via Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) Biosensing
item.description: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for trace-level analysis in complex systems owing to its nondestructive readout and molecular fingerprint information. However, direct and reliable SERS analysis remains challenging because signals from trace analytes are readily obscured by matrix interference and competitive adsorption, complicating analysis in complex biofluids. Here, we introduce a SERS sensing approach that amplifies spectral differences through a novel response...

item.title: Recent Chemical Advances in C-Glycosidic Ellagitannins
item.description: C-Glycosidic ellagitannins are a complex subclass of hydrolyzable tannins characterized by a carbon-carbon bond between the C-1 position of an open-chain d-glucose core and a hexahydroxydiphenoyl unit. Their architectures, featuring densely packed oxygen functionalities, multiple axes of chirality, and unique C-glycosidic linkages, render them formidable total-synthesis targets. This review traces the biomimetic strategies inspired by the biosynthetic pathways proposed in recent chemical...

item.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Feedback
item.description: Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its role within the TUR framework has remained unclear, particularly in quantum systems where control is inherently information driven. In this Letter, we consider open quantum systems weakly coupled to a...

item.title: Region-specific generation and retention of acetylated cohesin shape the genome-wide pattern of sister chromatid cohesion
item.description: Sister chromatid cohesion depends on ESCO2-mediated acetylation of the cohesin subunit SMC3, yet how this modification is established and maintained across the genome remains poorly understood. Here, we examined the chromatin-binding dynamics of ESCO2 and its enzymatic activity using quantitative ChIP-seq of human cells synchronously progressing through S phase. ESCO2 bound broadly along chromosomes without forming discrete peaks and preferentially localized to transcriptionally inactive...

item.title: Expanding the conjugation toolbox of DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters with biotin-streptavidin
item.description: DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-AgNCs) combine molecular-scale dimensions with sequence-dependent optical properties, making them promising candidates for bioimaging applications. However, strategies for site-specific conjugation of DNA-AgNCs remain comparatively limited. Here, we expand the conjugation toolbox of DNA-AgNCs through biotin functionalization of previously developed single-stranded DNA-AgNC containing a [Ag(16)Cl(2)]^(8+) cluster. Incorporation of biotin either at 3' end or...

item.title: Severe osteomalacia and insufficiency fractures due to combined iron induced hypophosphataemia and malabsorption-related calcium deficiency in a patient with Crohn's disease: A case report
item.description: Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) induced hypophosphataemia is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant adverse effect of intravenous iron therapy. In severe and prolonged cases, phosphate depletion may result in osteomalacia, insufficiency fractures, and significant functional impairment. However, longitudinal bone mineral density outcomes after treatment remain poorly documented. We report a 32-year-old woman with Crohn's disease and chronic iron deficiency anaemia who developed severe...

item.title: Surgical management of cecal volvulus using endoscopic reduction as a bridge to elective laparoscopic surgery: a three-case series
item.description: Cecal volvulus is a rare cause of bowel obstruction, typically managed by emergency surgery. Endoscopic reduction is generally not recommended due to its low success rate and risk of perforation. However, emergency surgery often requires laparotomy and may be associated with substantial surgical invasiveness. To reduce surgical invasiveness and avoid the risks associated with emergency surgery, we adopted a bridge-to-surgery strategy using endoscopic reduction followed by elective laparoscopic...

item.title: The perceived utility and scope of ecological momentary assessment and interventions for non-suicidal self-injury: A needs-based dynamic risk perspective
item.description: CONCLUSION: Integrating EMA and EMIs into treatment has potential to provide needs-tailored support for individuals who self-injure. Future work should focus on empirically validating the proposed dynamic model and co-designing EMI components that address fluctuating needs in daily life.

item.title: Revisiting extended-criteria donors in lung transplantation
item.description: Lung transplantation (LTx) is an established life-saving therapy for patients with end-stage lung disease. Despite continuous improvements in surgical technique, immunosuppressive regimen and perioperative care, organ shortage remains the principal limitation to broader access. Historically, conservative donor criteria have contributed to the underutilization of potentially transplantable lungs. Over time, lungs from donors outside standard criteria - commonly referred to as extended-criteria...

item.title: Acid-assisted water loss in perrhenate-catalysed deoxydehydration: an agent-assisted reaction-network search with microkinetic modelling
item.description: Perrhenate is the cheapest and most robust deoxydehydration (DODH) catalyst. Two decades of reports show that protic and acidic environments make it work, and no study has located where the proton acts. We answer that question by providing a predicted mechanism that is consistent with observed kinetics. The authors set the mechanistic hypotheses, and an AI agent located the corresponding transition states, which the authors then validated; solvent participation was resolved shell by shell,...

item.title: Toothpaste-Related Attitudes and Practices of Parents of Preschool Children in Istanbul, Türkiye: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Despite high overall rates of toothpaste usage, important gaps remain: delayed introduction, high rates of toothpaste swallowing among young children and critically low awareness of fluoride as a key toothpaste ingredient. Targeted parental education, particularly on the benefits of fluoridated toothpaste, appropriate quantity and correct post-brushing behaviour, is urgently needed.

item.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders
item.description: CONCLUSION: The framework provides a reproducible, rule-based, and modular tool for integrated EEG-ECG analysis of sleep microstructure and autonomic dynamics. By enabling synchronized CAP-HRV feature extraction in a single environment, it lowers the engineering barrier to brain-heart coupling research during sleep and provides a foundation for future extensions, including validated CAP detection, a matched-control study, a Python port, and cloud-based deployment.

item.title: Model-informed precision dosing of vancomycin and amikacin in critically ill neonates: a pre- and post-intervention study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Bayesian MIPD was associated with numerically but not statistically higher pharmacodynamic target attainment (AUC/MIC and Cmax/MIC) for vancomycin and amikacin, and no improvement in clinical outcomes was demonstrated. While amikacin modeling requires further refinement, adequately powered trials are needed to definitively assess the impact of MIPD on safety and clinical outcomes.

item.title: When the model defines the message: methodological considerations in experimental lung warm ischemia
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Interaction of sex and insulin resistance with cognitive impairment in community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher insulin resistance is a significant modifiable factor for cognitive impairment, specifically in women aged ≥65 years. These exploratory findings suggest potential sex-related differences in the metabolic-cognitive association, underscoring the importance of sex-specific metabolic management starting from midlife to help preserve cognitive health in later life.

item.title: Clinical Outcomes of Surgical Treatment for Crohn's Disease-Associated Duodenal Fistulas
item.description: Duodenal fistulas associated with Crohn's disease (CD) are extremely rare, with a reported incidence of only 0.5%-2%. Most arise secondarily from adjacent diseased bowels, such as the ileocecal region, transverse colon, or previous anastomotic sites. Because available reports are limited, the optimal surgical strategy remains unclear. Surgical management generally involves resection of the diseased bowel and appropriate repair of the duodenal defect, with decompression when appropriate.

item.title: RNA recognition and cleavage in archaeal ribosome biogenesis: insights from FAU-1
item.description: Ribosomal RNA maturation requires nucleases that recognize appropriate precursors and cleave them at defined stages of ribosome assembly. How these activities are organized in archaea remains elusive. Kawai and colleagues determined the crystal structure of the archaeal ribonuclease FAU-1, revealing a homotrimer with peripheral RNA-binding domains and a central assembly formed by its C-terminal domains. The structure identifies similarities to the RNA-recognition region of bacterial ribonuclease...

item.title: Balancing adaptive delivery and implementation fidelity over time: a longitudinal mixed-methods study of a community health worker-led adolescent nutrition intervention in rural Uganda
item.description: CONCLUSION: Adaptive delivery and implementation fidelity can be managed as interdependent implementation processes rather than competing priorities. Fidelity monitoring, supportive supervision, and guided problem-solving supported context-responsive delivery adjustments while supporting maintenance of core intervention functions.

item.title: The momentary associations of negative affect, anxiety and stress with symptoms in individuals with anorexia nervosa: a scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Negative affect, anxiety and stress are associated with disorder-specific cognitions and urges, though the translation into observable behaviour varies by context and subtype. Future research must address current gaps by adopting multi-modal assessments. Strengthening methodological consistency will be important for advancing the understanding of the interplay between affective states and symptoms in AN.

item.title: Effects of CytoSorb<sup>®</sup> hemoadsorption therapy on serum myoglobin and creatine kinase levels in severe rhabdomyolysis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Based on current limited evidence, this study suggests that CS therapy may be associated with reductions in circulating myoglobin concentrations in patients with severe rhabdomyolysis. However, the certainty of evidence is low, the effect on CK is unclear, and it remains to be determined if biochemical reductions in CK or myoglobin translate to improved clinical outcomes.

item.title: Optical response of surface-immobilized gold nanospheres on finite-thickness gold thin films
item.description: Surface-immobilized gold nanospheres (SIGNs) on a metal surface, also known as nanoparticle-on-a-film structures, constitute an efficient plasmonic platform that can be fabricated using bottom-up processes. These structures exhibit strong localized surface plasmon resonances. Although analytical solutions for the optical response of SIGNs on metals of semi-infinite thickness have been reported, no analytical method has been proposed for SIGNs on metal films of finite thickness. In this study, we...

item.title: Deep-ultraviolet second-harmonic generation in a three-coherence-length SrB<sub>4</sub>O<sub>7</sub> microcavity
item.description: We demonstrate deep-ultraviolet second-harmonic generation at 249.5 nm from a reflective vertical microcavity containing a SrB(4)O(7) layer three coherence lengths thick. With the fundamental beam blocked between settings, the second-harmonic signal showed near-quadratic power scaling. During uninterrupted upward power sweeps, the device exhibited a steeper, sweep-dependent response and reached a maximum observed average-power-normalized efficiency of 409% W^(-1)- approximately 157 times that of...

item.title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti-Ambipolar Characteristics in n-Type Organic Mixed-Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
item.description: Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio-realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long-term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti-ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti-ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic...

item.title: Management of acute situations in institutionalised Parkinsonian patients: A survey in Seine-Saint-Denis, France
item.description: CONCLUSION: PD and PS were frequently identified among residents of participating EHPADs, yet a substantial proportion of patients lack neurological follow-up. Emergency referrals and hospitalisations affected approximately one-quarter of patients, often for potentially preventable causes. These findings suggest that preventive strategies, multidisciplinary follow-up, and improved access to neurologists may help reduce avoidable hospitalisations.

item.title: Treatment Effect of Perioperative (Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant) Apalutamide plus Androgen-deprivation Therapy Versus Radical Prostatectomy Alone in Patients with High-risk Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer from the PROTEUS Substudy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative apalutamide plus ADT improved EFS and delayed subsequent therapy compared with SOC. Together with the blinded PROTEUS main study, these results support perioperative apalutamide plus ADT as a new therapeutic option for selected patients with HR-LPC/LAPC who are fit for surgery and 1-yr systemic therapy.

item.title: Mosunetuzumab as salvage therapy for refractory connective tissue diseases: clinical responses and immunological insights
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Proinflammatory strains of Mediterraneibacter gnavus are enriched during spondyloarthritis and bolster disease severity in animal model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SpA is associated with a distinct repertoire of MG strains characterised by increased adaptability to inflammatory stress and heightened proinflammatory and toxic potential. These findings establish a link between strain‑level microbial diversity and disease susceptibility.

item.title: Molecular response diversity of dissolved organic matter under ocean warming
item.description: How dissolved organic matter (DOM) composition varies along ocean temperature gradients is critical for understanding its role in future ocean carbon cycling. Here, we use a highly resolved dataset of over 800 DOM samples covering the surface waters to the deep Atlantic, Southern, and Pacific oceans to examine DOM thermal responses, defined as temperature-associated changes in DOM molecular relative abundance. item.description: It is commonly known that the Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) manipulates host gene expression to facilitate its reproduction. HSV-1 regulates host and viral transcription through coordinated effects on transcription factors, RNA polymerase II, transcription initiation and elongation, and host chromatin dynamics. However, how HSV-1 proteins regulate host histone chaperones and histone modifications remains incompletely understood. Here, we identified a functional relationship between the...

item.title: Phototherapy for Psoriasis in Contemporary, Biologic-Focused Practice
item.description: Phototherapy has been a cornerstone of psoriasis management since before the biologic era, and despite being eclipsed by systemic agents, it retains meaningful clinical utility. Narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) achieves clinically significant clearance rates, has been associated with greater improvement in overall health-related quality of life compared to adalimumab, and is effective across all skin tones. NB-UVB is associated with spatially distinct transcriptomic changes within plaques and...

item.title: Distributions, transport and environmental effects of BTEX along the Pearl River-estuary-ocean continuum
item.description: Benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene isomers (BTEX) are important anthropogenic pollutants with implications for coastal ecosystems and atmospheric chemistry. However, their land-ocean spatial gradients and transport remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated aquatic and atmospheric BTEX across the Pearl River Basin-Pearl River Estuary (PRE)-northeastern South China Sea (SCS) continuum. Surface BTEX concentrations in the PRE (198 ± 137 ng L^(-1)) were significantly higher than those...

item.title: Clinical Trials: A Call for Collaboration Between Pediatrics and Internal Medicine
item.description: The conduct of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in kidney disease among children and older youth has historically been challenging, reflecting, in part, the relative rarity of the conditions. This has resulted in a 13-year gap between the granting of approval for novel therapies in adults and their subsequent approval in children and created a significant lag in access to drugs in pediatrics that treat kidney disorders. One contributing factor that has been neglected is the operational barriers...

item.title: Family Risk and Resilience Patterns Differentiate Early Childhood Vulnerability to Intergenerational Transmission of Abdominal Pain
item.description: Children are at increased risk of developing chronic abdominal pain if a parent has an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction such as irritable bowel syndrome, suggesting family mechanisms of intergenerational pain transmission. However, patterns of family risk and resilience factors that predict children's vulnerability for developing chronic abdominal pain remain unknown. In a sample of parents with an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction and their young...

item.title: Integrated analysis of mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA expression profiles and regulatory relationships during longissimus dorsi muscle development in Lufeng cattle
item.description: Lufeng cattle (Bos taurus) are an indigenous breed of southern China with strong environmental adaptability but limited meat production performance. To characterize postnatal skeletal muscle development, longissimus dorsi samples were collected at 3 days, 4 months, and 24 months of age for integrated mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA sequencing. Nine libraries generated 545,665,884 clean reads, identifying 21,483 mRNAs, 1688 lncRNAs, and 18,147 circRNAs. Across pairwise comparisons, 1568 non-redundant...

item.title: VpsCDPK9 negatively regulates the salt and alkaline tolerance of grapevine by enhancing the reactive oxygen burst of VviRbohs
item.description: The grape industry, critical for rural economic development and farmer income, faces escalating challenges from soil salinization. Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are important calcium signaling components that have been shown to play crucial roles in modulating plant abiotic stress responses. item.title: Brain Regions Involved in Object-Location Memory in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review and Activation Likelihood Estimation Meta-Analysis of Task-Based fMRI
item.description: The ability to remember where objects are located is a fundamental cognitive function particularly vulnerable to aging and neurodegenerative disease. Previous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) research has combined object-location memory (OLM) with broader spatial-memory and -navigation tasks, resulting in inconsistent findings. This systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis isolated OLM to characterize brain regions engaged during...

item.title: Limited Evidence for Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation as a Cognitive Enhancer in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis of Sham-Controlled Trials
item.description: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) is increasingly applied to ameliorate cognitive deficits in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability, yet whether standardized scalp-based protocols produce reliable cognitive enhancement remains untested at scale. This study evaluates the transdiagnostic efficacy of NIBS on shared, non-core cognitive domains across NDDs, searching MEDLINE,...

item.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial adaptation and resilience of single-stage partial nitritation-anammox systems assisted by graphene oxide sponges under increasing salinity
item.description: Salinity is an increasingly important challenge limiting the application of single-stage partial nitritation-Anammox (PN/A) processes for treating saline nitrogen-rich wastewaters due to osmotic stress and microbial activity inhibition. In this study, a graphene oxide sponge (GOS)-assisted PN/A system was operated for 164 days under progressively increasing salinity from 2,000 to 12,000 mg/L NaCl to investigate the long-term performance and the associated physiological, ecological, and...

item.title: Is blastocyst culture failure during first IVF cycle a sign of poor prognosis in subsequent cycles? A matched case-control study
item.description: CONCLUSION: While initial failure is linked to lower oocyte yield and early embryo competence, it is not an absolute barrier to success. Most patients recover in subsequent cycles through protocol optimization, though diminished ovarian reserve remains the primary risk factor for recurrent failure. Our findings underscore the multifactorial nature of embryonic arrest and highlight potential clinical indicators for predicting and managing blastocyst development failure to optimize IVF success...

item.title: Yiqi Jiedu Formula Suppresses Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Growth in Association with Glycerophospholipid Metabolism Remodeling: An Integrated Metabolomics and Lipidomics Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: YQJDF treatment showed antitumor effects and was accompanied by extensive lipid metabolic remodeling in NPC tissues. Glycerophospholipid metabolism may represent an important metabolic pathway associated with YQJDF treatment, and several lipid-metabolism-related enzymes were identified as molecular candidates for further mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a basis for further validation of the role of lipid metabolic alterations in the antitumor response to YQJDF.

item.title: The Senescent Macrophage as a Central Hub in Skeletal Aging: Mechanisms, Niche Disruption, and Systemic Consequences
item.description: Bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) coordinate skeletal remodelling, haematopoietic niche function, immune surveillance, and tissue repair. Whether a persistent senescent state in BMMs is a causal driver of skeletal ageing, however, remains unresolved. The central challenge is both definitional and causal: macrophages may be quiescent, terminally differentiated, chronically activated, tolerant, or metabolically dysfunctional, whereas commonly used senescence markers-including p16^(INK4a), p21^(CIP1),...

item.title: Immunosenescence in radio-immunotherapy: from biological mechanisms to therapeutic opportunities?
item.description: Radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy across multiple cancer types. However, despite encouraging findings from selected clinical trials, most radioimmunotherapy studies have shown only limited or even negative results, highlighting important biological barriers that limit therapeutic efficacy. Accumulating evidence suggests that radiotherapy induces phenotypic and functional changes in immune cells that resemble key features of age-related...

item.title: Loss of GIPR in glutamatergic neurons does not impair acceleration of GLP-1-induced weight loss by GIPR antagonism
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our results show that GIPR antagonism does not require GIPR signaling in Vglut2-expressing neurons to potentiate GLP-1-induced weight loss, suggesting that the GIPR expressing cells/neurons mediating this effect are neither GABAergic nor Vglut2-expressing glutamatergic.

item.title: Methadone induces phospholipidosis and lysosomal dysfunction in astrocytes in vitro and in the developing brain
item.description: CONCLUSION: Methadone induces phospholipidosis and lysosomal dysfunction in astrocytes, accompanied by neuroinflammatory activation during brain development. These findings uncover an unrecognized mechanism linking methadone's amphiphilic properties to developmental neurotoxicity and emphasize the need to re-evaluate the safety of methadone use during pregnancy.

item.title: The xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase TaXTH16 enhances wheat drought tolerance and pre-harvest sprouting resistance via ABA-mediated pathways
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study establishes TaXTH16 as a positive regulator of wheat drought tolerance and PHS resistance, linking ABA signaling and cell wall remodeling. TaXTH16 is directly activated by TaABF2, and TaXTH16-2B-HapII represents a promising allele for breeding. These findings provide mechanistic insights into ABA-cell wall crosstalk and a valuable resource for improving wheat stress resilience.

item.title: Development and validation of the OpENS model for upper gastrointestinal cancer screening across diverse regions in China

item.title: Effect of electroconvulsive therapy on anhedonia in adults with major depressive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ECT was associated with a statistically significant improvement in anhedonia among adults with MDD.
